questions.question: Is texting while driving a CMV illegal?

options.text: No, it is okay on rural roads.
No, it is okay when contacting your employer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, it is illegal.
questions.explanation: Texting while driving is dangerous and illegal for all CMV drivers.

questions.question: What should you do if you must drive slowly and block other drivers?
questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your four-way flashers.
questions.explanation: When driving slowly and blocking traffic, turn on your four-way flashers to warn drivers behind you (if local laws allow it).

questions.question: What does a posted speed limit mean?

options.text: It can be exceeded when passing.
It can be exceeded in rural areas.

questions.correctAnswerText: It should never be exceeded.
questions.explanation: The posted speed limit is the maximum speed allowed under ideal conditions. Slow down when conditions require it. Never exceed the legal speed limit.

questions.question: Which tire condition is NOT a problem that needs fixing?

options.text: Front tires with tread depth of at least 4/32 inch

questions.correctAnswerText: Front tires with tread depth of at least 4/32 inch
questions.explanation: Check tires for: wrong air pressure; mixing radial and bias-ply tires; front tire tread less than 4/32 inch; and other tire tread less than 2/32 inch. Tires with 4/32 inch tread are acceptable.

questions.question: How often must hazmat employees be trained?

options.text: At least once every three years

questions.correctAnswerText: At least once every three years
questions.explanation: Hazmat employees must be trained and tested at least once every three years.

questions.question: Are height warnings always posted on low bridges?

options.text: Yes, they must always be posted.
Yes, they must be posted at least twice.
No, they may or may not be posted.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, they may or may not be posted.
questions.explanation: Height warnings are often posted on low bridges, but not always. Drive slowly if you are unsure you can clear an overhead object.

questions.question: How should cargo in a trailer be handled?

options.text: It does not need to be secured.
It should be stacked no more than three feet high.
It should be secured to prevent movement.

questions.correctAnswerText: It should be secured to prevent movement.
questions.explanation: Cargo must be properly secured so it does not shift during transport.

questions.question: What should you do when construction workers are near the road?
questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: In work zones, follow posted speed limits. Reduce your speed further when workers are on or near the road.

questions.question: Which exhaust system condition should NOT concern you?

options.text: Exhaust parts rubbing against fuel system parts

questions.correctAnswerText: Exhaust parts made of aluminum
questions.explanation: Check exhaust systems for: loose or missing pipes and mufflers; loose or missing brackets and bolts; parts rubbing against fuel or tires; and leaking parts. Aluminum parts are not a concern.

questions.question: What does it mean if brakes pull to one side when used?
questions.correctAnswerText: They need to be checked.
questions.explanation: Brakes that pull to one side indicate a brake problem that needs to be fixed.

questions.question: When you start a vehicle:

options.text: Warning lights should turn on briefly, then turn off.

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning lights should turn on briefly, then turn off.
questions.explanation: When you start your engine, warning lights should appear and then turn off quickly. If they stay on, there is a problem with your vehicle.

questions.question: Driving at night is usually:

options.text: Harder than driving during the day.
Easier than driving during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Harder than driving during the day.
questions.explanation: Driving at night is harder for several reasons. You cannot see hazards as well, headlight glare affects your vision, and tired drivers are more common on the road at night.

questions.question: You should use your mirrors:

options.text: With a helper watching your blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Often while driving.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors frequently while driving, especially the mirrors on both sides of your vehicle.

questions.question: Stopping distance can be affected by:

options.text: How many passengers are in the car.
What time of day it is.

questions.correctAnswerText: How fast you are going.
questions.explanation: Stopping distance is affected by your vehicle's speed, its weight, and how slippery the road is.

questions.question: Who must label hazardous materials?
questions.correctAnswerText: The shipper
questions.explanation: The shipper is responsible for packing, marking, and labeling hazardous materials. They must also provide any required placards.

questions.question: A driver should make sure that:

options.text: The shipping papers match the markings and labels on the packages.
The shipping papers are written in code.
All packages are labeled as poison.

questions.correctAnswerText: The shipping papers match the markings and labels on the packages.
questions.explanation: Compare the markings and labels on packages with the shipping papers. Make sure the shipper wrote the correct description on the papers and put the right labels on the packages.

questions.question: What are baffled liquid tanks?

options.text: Tanks with dividers that have holes to let liquid flow through
Tanks that let liquid move freely with no dividers inside
Tanks with nothing inside to slow liquid flow

questions.correctAnswerText: Tanks with dividers that have holes to let liquid flow through
questions.explanation: Baffled tanks have dividers with holes inside them. These dividers stop the liquid from surging forward and backward, while the holes let liquid move between sections.

questions.question: What is black ice?

options.text: A thick layer of ice on the road
A thin layer of ice on the road
Ice that looks black because of dirt on the road
Ice that is easy to see

questions.correctAnswerText: A thin layer of ice on the road
questions.explanation: Black ice is a thin, clear layer of ice. You can see the road through it, so it can look like the road is just wet.

questions.question: When checking your tires, you do not want to see:

options.text: Tire tread that is 4/32 of an inch deep.

questions.correctAnswerText: Different tire sizes.
questions.explanation: Front tires should have at least 4/32 inch of tread depth, and other tires need at least 2/32 inch. Valve stems should not be cut or cracked. All tires should be the same size.

questions.question: Which of these does NOT show bad brakes?

options.text: Pads that are clean and dry

questions.correctAnswerText: Pads that are clean and dry
questions.explanation: When checking your brakes, watch for cracked drums, shoes or pads covered in oil or grease, and shoes that are worn too thin or broken.
